subject: Price equalization & technical handover for SignalWorks replacement
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@signalworks.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@signalworks.com, Michael Hsu <michael.hsu@signalworks.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring replacement options — pricing parity & technical handover

Hi Diego,

We ran a quick internal review and we think there's a reasonable chance we can consolidate away from our current vendor this quarter. Before we go deeper, procurement and engineering asked for two things from Redwood:

1) A clear price-equalization proposal that shows net-first-year economics (credits, seat bundling, and any one-time migration concessions).
2) A short technical handover note confirming runtime compatibility (KV cache export/import, model format support, and any required client changes).

I attached the current term sheet we have with our incumbent so you can see the headline structure. Can you confirm whether Redwood can match on a TTM basis or if you need to propose a structured bridge? Also, who on your side owns the technical path for data/weights compatibility?

Our timeline is aggressive — procurement would like an initial commercial counter by EOD Friday so we can loop legal.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations
SignalWorks

Attached: signalworks-term-sheet-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@signalworks.com>
Cc: procurement@signalworks.com, Michael Hsu <michael.hsu@signalworks.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement options — pricing parity & technical handover

Hi Lena — appreciate the context and the term sheet. Short answers up front: yes, we can put together a price-equalization package plus a migration concession; and Connor (cc'd) will own the technical review + compatibility plan.

High-level commercial approach we propose now:
- First-year bridge: up to 30% gross credit applied as usage credit over the first 12 months, structured as staged drawdowns tied to monthly MRR/usage.
- Seat bundling: ability to map legacy seats to our "Runtime-Plus" seat bundle (discounted token rates + priority capacity).
- One-time migration support: engineering hours on us for data transfer and a short pilot to prove parity.

I've attached a replacement matrix that maps the incumbent's line items to Redwood SKUs so you can see the gaps. This is a working draft — Marissa will confirm commercial flexibility.

Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk the matrix and agree mutual action items. Does that work?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-replacement-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, stub)

Forwarding Diego's note and adding commercial detail from my side.

Lena / Michael — welcome, and excited by the opportunity. A few commercial clarifications from Redwood's side:

- We can commit to a price-equalization package that matches material TCO for year 1 when combined with the migration credits. Exact percentages depend on committed usage bands; for an initial alignment assume 25-30% effective first-year credit for a 12-month pilot + a 12-month renewable agreement.
- We prefer staged credits (drawn against usage) rather than upfront rebates to keep incentives aligned; we can do an upfront buy-down if procurement requires it.
- Legal: we can accept the incumbents' SLAs as a baseline but need carveouts for custom quantization profiles and capacity reservations.

Attached is a short concession-terms draft that outlines the credit mechanics and rollback protections for both sides. If procurement agrees, we can memorialize this as a term sheet and hand to legal.

Diego / Connor — please prepare a short tech note confirming what's required to port KV state and how we handle model artifacts.

Next steps: 1) confirm whether staged drawdown is acceptable; 2) procurement to send a list of mandatory security/compliance artifacts; 3) book pilot kickoff for the following week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi all — Connor from Solutions here. Quick technical clarifications and a suggested packaging option: 

1) Runtime compatibility: we support the same model container formats you currently use; KV cache can be exported as a set of sharded protobuf bundles we ingest into our runtime with no heavy re-serialization. We will own a small compatibility shim for any bespoke model artifacts.

2) Security: SOC2 Type II plus dedicated KMS integration is supported; we can provide a limited KMS-HSM diagram and an attestation letter for key custody.

3) Packaging suggestion (explicit pricing example):
- "Runtime-Plus" bundle: priority capacity + 10% token discount + 40 hours migration engineering included. Effective token rate for your current volumes ~ $0.0009/token after credits (example banding shown in attached matrix).

4) Pilot plan: 4-week technical pilot, milestone-driven (week 1 ingest + parity tests, week 2 baseline benchmarks, weeks 3–4 shadow traffic + cutover runbook).

I'll attach a compact runtime compatibility matrix and a draft Mutual Action Plan link. If procurement can accept the staged credits model, we can map that directly into the pilot acceptance gates.

Next actions: Diego/Marissa to confirm commercial banding; Michael/Lena to confirm procurement checklist items needed for legal. I'll be available for a 30-min call Monday to walk the pilot plan.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
